findings.title: test
findings.text: This test can pass for the wrong reason. The migrator refuses with exit 1 not only when `pins_hold` flags the contradiction, but also via the `judged < expected` guard ("only N of M migrated pin(s) were judged") when `without_applicability` fails to make the claim apply. A regression in that stripping (the exact behavior this test is meant to pin) would still leave exit 1 and an unchanged snapshot, so the stated property ("the contradiction is found despite the selector") is not actually asserted. Pin the failure's identity the way test (b) does.

findings.title: test
findings.text: Every "nothing written" proof (tests b, c, d, e) uses a single-file corpus, so the multi-file path is never exercised. The tool currently verifies all planned files in one scratch copy before writing any, which is what makes a refused mixed corpus leave `claims/` untouched; but a regression to per-file verify-and-write would still pass every existing test (the one good file is written, then the bad one aborts). Add a fixture with one valid and one contradicted claim and assert exit 1 plus a whole-directory unchanged snapshot — that is the case that distinguishes the two designs (and the duplicate-name refusal in `verify_output`).

findings.title: bug
findings.text: `run_req` runs an arbitrary `req` found on `PATH` with no `timeout`, and `capture_output=True` buffers unbounded output. A hung `canon`/`gate` (or a corpus large enough to stall the pipe) blocks the migration forever, with no way to tell it apart from a slow run. Pass a `timeout=` and translate `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` (and `UnicodeDecodeError` from `text=True`) into `Unverifiable`, so the tool still exits 3 with "nothing written".

findings.title: bug
findings.text: Scratch setup (`copytree`, `makedirs`, and the `open` inside `put`) can raise `OSError` (permissions, disk full, `TemporaryDirectory` cleanup). `run` only catches `Refused`/`Unverifiable`, so those escape as a raw traceback rather than the documented clean refusal/UNVERIFIABLE that writes nothing. Wrap the scratch build (and `put`) in `try/except OSError` and raise `Unverifiable`.
